strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with per-stage scaling
strategies.desc: Perform 8 sequential all-reduce operations (xm.all_reduce) with elementwise scaling and division between each stage, exactly as in the reference implementation. Total dispatch count is 8 all-reduces. This is the baseline: simplest structure but no fusion of local operations with collectives.

strategies.name: Fused scale-reduce with single buffer
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all scaling coefficients and fuse the scale/divide operations into vectorized operations on the full buffer before each all-reduce, eliminating intermediate clones by reusing a single buffer. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces memory allocations and potentially enables compiler fusion of elementwise ops into fewer kernels.

strategies.name: Chunked reduce-scatter then all-gather pattern
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, operating on 224 chunks of size 256. Each of the 8 stages becomes 2 collectives (16 total dispatches). Trades more dispatches for potentially better network utilization at world_size=224 by exploiting bandwidth-optimal RS+AG decomposition.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapping computation and communication
strategies.desc: Partition the 224 shards into groups and pipeline the scaling computation with all-reduce operations across stages, launching the next stage's all-reduce on completed portions while current stage finishes. Requires 8+ dispatches with careful buffer management but can hide computation latency behind communication.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction per stage
strategies.desc:
Decompose each of the 8 all-reduce operations into intra-node reduce followed by inter-node all-reduce, assuming multi-node topology (num_nodes parameter). Results in 16 collective dispatches (2 per stage × 8 stages) but exploits faster intra-node communication fabric and reduces inter-node traffic volume.
